sanskrit: indra juṣasvā yāhi śūra pibā sutasya madhoś cakānaḥ | cārur madāya ||
english: O Indra, be pleased and come, O hero; drink of the pressed honey-mead, delighting in it — charming for exhilaration.

sanskrit: ā tvā viśantu sutāsa indra pṛṇasva kukṣī viḍḍhi śakra | dhiyehy ā naḥ ||
english: Let the pressed Soma-draughts enter into you, O Indra; fill your belly, strengthen yourself, O Śakra — come hither to our devotions.

sanskrit: indra jaṭharaṃ pṛṇasva madhor asya sutasya | upa tvā madeṣu vājo astu ||
english: O Indra, fill your belly with this pressed honey-mead; may vigour attend you in your states of rapture.

sanskrit: indras turāṣāḍ jaghāna vṛtraṃ sāsāha śatrūn samatsu vajrī | made somasya ||
english: Indra the irresistible conqueror smote Vṛtra; the wielder of the vajra overcame enemies in battles — in the rapture of Soma.

sanskrit: śrudhī havaṃ me giro juṣasva- -indra svayugbhiḥ matsva madāya | mahe raṇāya ||
english: Hear my invocation, be pleased with my hymns, O Indra; exhilarate yourself with your own teams for rapture — for great battle.

sanskrit: ud itye akraman trayo vyāghraḥ puruṣo vṛkaḥ | hirug jyotiḥ sūryo hirug devo vanaspatir hiruṅ navantu śatravaḥ ||
english: Up have stepped these three: the tiger, the man, the wolf. The light is turned away, the sun is turned away, the god Vanaspati is turned away — may the enemies be turned away.

sanskrit: parameṇa pathā vṛkaḥ pareṇa steno arṣatu | tato vyāghraḥ paramaḥ ||
english: Let the wolf rush away by the farthest path, let the thief rush away by the far path; the tiger is the most distant of all.

sanskrit: akṣyau ca te hanū ca te vyāghra jambhayāmasi | āt sarvān viṃśatiṃ nakhān ||
english: Both your eyes and your jaws, O tiger, we crush; and therewith all your twenty claws.

sanskrit: yat saṃnaśo vi yan naśo yad ?vinaśo na saṃ naśaḥ? | mūrṇā mṛgasya dantā apiśīrṇā u pṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: Whatever has come together is scattered, whatever has scattered does not come together again — blunted are the beast's teeth, and its ribs are shattered.

sanskrit: vyāghraṃ datvatāṃ vayaṃ prathamaṃ jambhayāmasi | ād it stenam ahiṃ yātudhānam atho vṛkam ||
english: We crush first the tiger that tears with its teeth; and therewith the thief, the serpent, the sorcerer, and also the wolf.

sanskrit: neva rapsasai na gṛhaḥ paraś cara | dvipāc catuṣpān no mā hiṃsīr indrajāḥ somajā asi ||
english: Do not seize upon, do not enter the house; go far away. Do not harm our bipeds and our quadrupeds — you are born of Indra, born of Soma.

sanskrit: iyaṃ vīrun madhujātā madhune tvā khanāmasi | madhor adhi prajātāsi sā no madhumatas kṛdhi ||
english: This herb, honey-born, we dig up for honey's sake; you have sprung forth from honey — make us rich in honey.

sanskrit: jihvāyā agre me madhu jihvāmūle madhūlakam | yathā māṃ kāminy aso yathā mām anv āyasi ||
english: At the tip of my tongue be honey, at the root of my tongue a honey-sweet — so that you may be impassioned for me, so that you may come after me.

sanskrit: pari tvā paritatnunā- -ikṣuṇāgām avidviṣe | yathā na vidviṣāvahai na vibhavāva kadā cana ||
english: I have come around you with the encircling sugarcane, for freedom from enmity — so that we two may never be hostile to each other, may never part from each other at any time.

sanskrit: rājñe brūhi varuṇāya- -aśvāya puruṣāya ca | pathā me pathye revati jāyām ā vaha sādhunā ||
english: Speak to King Varuṇa, and to the horse, and to the man — by the prosperous, auspicious path, O Pathyā Revatī, bring the wife to me by a good road.

sanskrit: jāyāṃ me mitrāvaruṇā jāyāṃ devī sarasvatī | jāyāṃ me aśvinobhā- -ā dhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
english: May Mitra and Varuṇa grant me a wife; may the goddess Sarasvatī grant me a wife; may both the Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, bestow a wife upon me.
